newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Hamas party changes name.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Hamas party changes name.

text.p: Algeria's main legal Islamist party Hamas announced on Sunday it was changing its name to conform to a new law banning political parties based on Islam.

Party leader Mahfoud Nahnah told a news conference in party headquarters in Algiers that the Movement of the Islamic Society -- known by its acronym Hamas -- was now named Movement of a Peaceful Society.
Party officials, speaking by telephone, said the interior ministry had agreed as long as party leaders use the full name, since the acronym in Arabic of the new name still spells Hamas.

The change cleared a legal hurdle for the party to take part in Algeria's June 5 parliamentary elections. Nahnah won a third of the vote in 1995 presidential elections that returned President Liamine Zeroual to power.
Algeria in February banned political platforms based on religion. A general election in 1992 was cancelled when the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) were poised to win.
Algeria's other legal Islamist party in February renamed itself Nahda Movement from the former Nahda Islamic Movement.
The two groups are among about 30 parties preparing to compete for the 380-seat National Assembly election. The FIS is outlawed.
Algeria has been without a parliament since 1992. About 60,000 people have died since then in violence between Moslem guerrillas and government forces.
